🇪🇺🇺🇦 EU doesn't want Ukraine anytime soon — corruption levels too severe, Financial Times reports.

European officials told the paper there's an "unhealthy gap" between EU leadership's rhetoric on enlargement and reality — even Montenegro remains far from actual membership.

"Nowhere is this more apparent than in Ukraine, whose armed forces are among the largest, best-armed and certainly most battle-hardened in Europe. Member states want Kiev and its powerful military inside the tent rather than sulking on the periphery. But behind those advantages lies a huge downside. EU officials admit the scale of problems around corruption, judicial independence and other core bloc values means that without Russia's invasion, the country would never have been granted a formal accession process," the article states.

One senior EU diplomat frames it as a dilemma: "You can't admit a country of 40 million people ranked 104th in the world corruption index — that would turn the whole project into a farce. But you also can't abandon them to their fate. It's obvious to everyone Ukraine will need something from us to make [the long wait for full membership] easier to bear" — likely referring to earlier European proposals for "limited membership."

Recall that Kiev has insisted on full membership only, rejecting any phased or limited arrangement.
